title: MSR-ERO Low Gain Antenna (LGA)
description:
The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO X Band LGA unit it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Low Gain Antenna function is to provide simultaneously:
-	Signal radiation, i.e. conversion from guided transmission (waveguide I/F) to radiated waveform in X band downlink frequency band
-	Signal reception, i.e. conversion from radiated waveform to guided transmission to guided transmission (waveguide I/F) in X band uplink frequency band
The LGA shall operate in the following bands:
-	Uplink band: 7145 - 7190 MHz 
-	Downlink band: 8400 - 8450 MHz 

The LGA shall also provide a peak gain of between 6 and 8dBi and a coverage of +/-90° off-boresight.

title: Sada bezpilotních letadel
description: Předmětem zakázky je dodávka sady čtyř bezpilotních letadel a příslušenství. První letadlo disponuje vysokou nosností 7 kg pro transport nákladu a těžkého vybavení; druhé letadlo střední nosností 2,5 kg, senzorikou pro let uvnitř budov, podporou technologie RTK GNSS a širokou podporou příslušenství; třetí letadlo schopností napájení kabelem a statického optického monitoringu (virtuální stožár); čtvrté letadlo má nízkou vzletovou hmotnost a senzoriku vhodnou pro leteckou fotogrammetrii včetně RTK GNSS. title: COMBINED COMMUNICATIONS AND PNT USER TERMINAL DEVELOPMENT - EXPRO PLUS
description: The LightShip mission envisions deploying passenger spacecraft in Low Mars Orbit equipped with a User Terminal (UT) to access communications and position, navigation and timing (PNT) services. Developing a combined communications and PNT terminal would reduce size and mass, benefiting both spacecraft and overall mission efficiency, while also offering applicability to future deep space and lunar missions. The objective is to design a modular hardware architecture adaptable to various mission profiles, including transfer, orbital, lander, and surface operations. The software will include generic components alongside a customizable navigation engine, with a focus on real-time reduced dynamic solutions for demanding scenarios such as Mars transfer and orbiting. The activity will alsovalidate navigation techniques combining one-way and two-way measurements to improve accuracy and timing. Ground Support Equipment will be developed to test system performance under simulated Mars conditions, supporting hardware and software design, manufacturing,testing, and future flight model development.
